college noun

also colleges, sixth-form college, college of a university

Renaissance

Traupman 28, 293
M-O s.v. department7: college (within a university)
M-O s.v. school types: university: college, after Tursellinus (1652)

collēgium, collēgiī n.

noun, second declension

a college: of a university, or a school for older students

Classically a body of colleagues, a board or guild: mercātōrum collēgium īnstituere (Liv. 2.27.5). The Jesuits called their schools collēgia, though these gave no degrees, and the colleges of Oxford and Cambridge are collēgia too (Morgan–Owens). An American college, which is a university, is ūniversitās studiōrum or acadēmīa (see university).

See also university, student, school, education.
